newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU grain export commitments up on last year.
newsitem.headline: EU grain export commitments up on last year.

text.p: Latest European Union figures show grain export commitments between July 1 and December 10, 1996 were 11 percent above their year-ago level, mostly the result of higher wheat and barley sales, member-country officials said on Friday.
The figures, based on delivered export certificates, showed grain exports ahead on last year at 13.627 million tonnes against 12.260 million.
Commercial wheat export commitments reached 4.426 million tonnes up from 4.194 million during the same period last year.
Commercial barley exports jumped to 2.996 million tonnes from 1.161 million tonnes during the same period last year, helped by sales to Saudi Arabia.
Flour exports were ahead on last year at 2.917 million tonnes against 2.862 million.
Malt exports fell to 1.797 million tonnes from 2.181 million.
Commercial oats commitments reached 210,000 tonnes against 30,000 tonnes during the same period last year.

Since December 10, the EU has granted 477,700 tonnes of soft wheat, 76,550 tonnes of barley, 2,000 tonnes of rye, 2,500 tonnes of oats and 13,400 tonnes of durum wheat exports through its weekly grain tender system.
EU trade firms also showed contracts on December 11 to export a total 568,000 tonnes of soft wheat to a target group of African countries under a special long-term relief scheme.
